name: Stillhand — The Analog Craft Revival
description: Stillhand practitioners reject automated fabrication and BCI-assisted creation in favor of exclusively hand-made goods — pottery, hand-set type, woven textiles, blown glass, hand-bound books — produced without digital assistance of any kind. Unlike the Unclocked's ideological BCI refusal, Stillhand is craft-focused and largely apolitical: members may use BCIs in daily life but consider the making space sacred from digital intervention. Their hub, the Stillhand Workshop Collective in Tier 3's Pilsen Remnant district, runs twelve-week apprenticeships that have eighteen-month waiting lists. Finished goods are marked with a pressed thumbprint seal and command extraordinary prices in Tier 4-5 markets.
cultural_impact: Stillhand goods have become a Tier 4-5 luxury status symbol, creating uncomfortable tension within the movement between its working-class craft origins and the wealthy collectors who now dominate demand. 'Stillhand authentic' certification has been forged, spawning a verification cottage industry.
locations: Stillhand Workshop Collective, Pilsen Remnant, Tier 3
The Pressed Page (hand-letterpress shop), Milwaukee Corridor
story_hooks: A master Stillhand potter discovers her most celebrated piece was partially fabricated by an apprentice using a hidden nano-assembler — exposing it would destroy the apprentice's career and the collective's reputation.
A Tier 5 collector pays an enormous sum for a Stillhand piece, then commissions a forgery ring to flood the market — the collective must authenticate their own work without digital tools.
A Stillhand apprentice on the waiting list discovers that wealthy applicants are jumping the queue through back-channel payments to a senior member.
